messages:
sam: Heads-up — seeing a spike of 429s from dedicated pool ap-sg-reserved-1 starting ~07:05 UTC. Queue depth jumped and tail latency is climbing.
maya: on it. pulling metrics from the scheduler and reserved-pool exporter.
maya: quick query: `sum(reserved_pool_queue_depth{pool=\"ap-sg-reserved-1\"}) by (pool)` -> 1187 at 07:12 UTC
jonas: Oof. Any recent rollouts or scaling changes to that pool?
lisa: No rollouts. We did change admission policy yesterday (fairshare weight tweak) but only for eu-west pools.
capacity-bot: pool_status ap-sg-reserved-1 available_gpus=6 total_gpus=32 pending_jobs=342 oldest_job_age=00:12:34
ops-oncall: @maya can you check node health (OOMs, GPU ECC, network RX/TX)? If nodes are flapping, we should cordon.
maya: grabbing kube events now. seeing multiple `PodEvicted` due to node taint `gpu-pressure=true` on node ap-sg-03
maya: logs from node ap-sg-03:
```
[07:08:45] kubelet: eviction signal: ephemeral-storage or memory pressure
[07:08:46] nvidia-smi: GPU 0 ECC error count rising
```
jonas: ECC suggests hardware fault. ap-sg-03 is a dedicated rack. If it's 1 of 4 GPUs degraded, it can reduce pool effective capacity and push queues up.
lisa: we should drain ap-sg-03 and mark as degraded in capacity manager. Meanwhile, can we route lower-priority committed traffic to hosted fallback?
sam: Agreed. Actionables: 1) cordon+drain ap-sg-03; 2) apply temporary routing rule to send tier=burst and low-priority to hosted small-models; 3) throttle non-SLA tenants on the pool.
ops-oncall: i'm executing the cordon now: `kubectl cordon node/ap-sg-03` — done. Starting drain: `kubectl drain node/ap-sg-03 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` (progressing)
capacity-bot: admission_controller: pool ap-sg-reserved-1 rate_limit set from 1600 qps -> 900 qps (auto-scaling protection)
maya: after cordon, pending_jobs dropped a bit but queue still >900. Drain will take ~8-10m for long-running sessions.
sam: Routing change: adding fallback policy to route `policy: burst-fallback -> hosted/fast-sm` for requests with priority <= 50. pushing now.
jonas: pushed routing. Creating a short-lived canary for 10% traffic first. monitor error budget and latency.
maya: canary started — 10% of priority<=50 traffic now hitting hosted-sm. Seeing 20% reduction in pool queue depth after 2m.
lisa: cost note: hosted fallback will add ~0.7c/token for the overflow. We should track committed vs overage to billing.
sam: We should also open a hardware ticket for ap-sg-03 with infra-hw. tagging oncall-hw and scheduling replacement during low-traffic window.
ops-oncall: draining complete on ap-sg-03. pods evicted: 12. cluster autoscaler not adding nodes because pool is reserved capacity — need manual lift if we want temp extra GPUs.
jonas: manual lift request sent to provisioning: `REQ-2026-542` — asking for +4 GPUs in ap-sg-reserved-1 as burst capacity.
maya: monitoring: 95p latency down from 1200ms -> 420ms since canary routing and cordon. queue depth now 420.
sam: good progress. Next steps: confirm replacement of ap-sg-03, keep admission throttle at 900 qps for 30m, continue canary at 10% and escalate to 25% if steady.
lisa: I'll update SLO dashboard and add cost delta in the incident doc. also logging the fallback for audit (customer-impact tags).
ops-oncall: FYI — temporary mitigation means some non-SLA traffic will see model variance; notify support with template: `incident: dedicated-fanout-congestion -> fallback-hosted` :thumbsup:
sam: filing incident ticket IC-2026-123 and adding runbook steps + follow-ups. Thanks team. :raised_hands:
capacity-bot: incident_assigned IC-2026-123 severity=high owner=sam
maya: will keep monitoring for 30m and then reassess. If node replacement ETA >1h, prioritize adding burst GPUs.
sam: ack. closing live thread; will update later with postmortem notes and cost impact.
